clue.text: Small island bird's no female

indicators.note: the bird is said to have no female, so the letter for female is taken away

parts.note: a finch is a small bird; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A note about a little island whose bird population has no hens.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish place-name word for a small islet, found in names like Inchkeith.

clue.text: Absence of spirit in drink — I finally add it only at the end

parts.note: taken as written
to sip is to drink a little

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word add

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at the end picks the closing letter of the word only

explanation.surface: A barman's instruction: put the liquor in last, and only at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts as alcohol, matching 'drink', but it means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dullness and lack of flavour or liveliness is the condition named.

clue.text: Sigh for Conservative party

parts.note: a rave is a big dance party

explanation.surface: A Tory longs wistfully for a party, perhaps a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: To sigh for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: Sky watcher Moore's excited with North Star

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so these are rearranged

parts.note: the name Moore as written; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Patrick Moore, the famous TV stargazer, thrilled by the Pole Star.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Patrick Moore presented the BBC astronomy programme The Sky at Night for over fifty years, so the surface is nearly self-describing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies stars and planets watches the heavens professionally.

clue.text: Slow debate lets on law must change

indicators.note: the letters are required to change their order

explanation.surface: A legislator's complaint that, once revealed, a law has to be amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow' is a verb here: to stall a debate by obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstructing parliamentary business by delaying tactics is what the verb means.

clue.text: Diner's last to eat out and nearly be sick

indicators.note: the last of the word Diner's gives its final letter before the apostrophe

parts.note: acid etches, eating out a design in metal

explanation.surface: A diner's final reaction to eating out: almost throwing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave or gag without vomiting is very nearly being ill.

clue.text: Candidate put forward no note of maiden name

parts.note: taken as written
MI is a note of the sol-fa scale
née introduces a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A candidate puts herself forward without noting her maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone proposed for an office or award is a proposed candidate.

clue.text: Metal hand on Hindu god cut off by English

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes above it

parts.note: to man something is to work it, and a hand is a worker

indicators.note: cut off means the god's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Ganesh is the elephant-headed Hindu god

explanation.surface: A metal hand placed on a statue of a Hindu god, broken off by an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard grey metallic chemical element, used in steel alloys.

clue.text: Deceptive tactic is difficult to understand in the second half

indicators.note: only the latter half of the word for obscure is kept, its front half dropped

parts.note: abstruse means hard to grasp

explanation.surface: A sports pundit saying a team's trick play was baffling after the break.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'second half' sounds like a match period; it is the back four letters of an eight-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick or stratagem meant to deceive is a ploy.

clue.text: Engineers introducing principal cable stay

indicators.note: the engineers come first and introduce what follows

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
a main is the principal cable or pipe in a supply network

explanation.surface: Engineers fitting the main stay cable on a bridge or mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable stay' reads as one engineering thing; split it, and stay is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to stop on, continuing in the same place.

clue.text: One who's blamed son getting jacket split by a pin

indicators.note: the jacket word is split open and the other pieces put inside

parts.note: a coat is a jacket
a peg is a pin, as in a tent peg

explanation.surface: A boy whose jacket gets torn by a pin, and he takes the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A person made to bear the blame for others is the fall guy.

clue.text: Save millions in America

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)
taken as written
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A financial headline: Americans putting millions into savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' is the preposition meaning 'except', not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition, save means except, without or less.

clue.text: High churchman concerned with cutting gold and silver vessels

indicators.note: cutting means one piece slices into the other, landing inside it

parts.note: plate is the collective name for gold or silver tableware and church vessels
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A senior cleric whose interests are the church's treasures of gold and silver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop, abbot or other senior ecclesiastic is a dignitary of the church.

clue.text: Put up with stripped-down barn in which to store vehicles

parts.note: to hang a picture is to put it up

indicators.note: stripped down to its core, the word barn loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Tolerating a stripped-out old barn used for storing vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate, but 'with' is only a link; the vehicles are aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A large shed for housing aircraft is a building for keeping flying craft.

clue.text: Label is a source of music genre

parts.note: a stereo is a music system
a genre is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A record label as the origin of a musical style.
explanation.definitionFit: To label someone is to typecast them by a fixed, oversimplified image.

clue.text: Detective Inspector told to go with crook intended for hearing and setting free

parts.note: DI is the police rank Detective Inspector

indicators.note: for hearing means the words are as they sound when spoken

parts.words: told to go with crook intended
parts.note: told to go is sent, a crook or bend is an angle, and intended is meant; said together they make the last part

explanation.surface: A detective ordered to work with a villain for his court hearing, then released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a trial, setting up the crook and the detective; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing something from a tangle or snare frees it, the noun for that freeing.

clue.text: Sow recent strains for maize crop

indicators.note: strains means the letters are strained and twisted into new shape

explanation.surface: A farmer sowing newly bred strains of maize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strains' looks like plant varieties; it is the verb meaning to twist or distort.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize grown for its sweet kernels eaten as a vegetable is the crop named.

clue.text: Alcohol from fermenting celery with gin

indicators.note: fermenting means the letters are bubbling and changing

explanation.surface: A home brew: booze made by fermenting celery and gin together.
explanation.walkthrough: Alcohol here is the chemical class; glycerine is a trihydric alcohol, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically it is an alcohol with three hydroxyl groups, though not drinkable liquor.

clue.text: They've all shifted away from hearing a criminal case

indicators.note: shifted means these letters are moved about

parts.note: off means away from, as in off the coast
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Everyone has moved out of earshot of a criminal trial.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the Sherlock Holmes novel by Arthur Conan Doyle, a criminal case for the detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names one of Holmes's investigations, a case of crime solved.

clue.text: Top player on board nearly let in rook taking on a learner

indicators.note: nearly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to admit someone is to let them in
R is the chess notation for rook
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A chess game: the top player almost allows a rook in, then a novice joins.
explanation.walkthrough: The chessboard is a decoy: the board is a ship's deck, its top player the fleet commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy's highest-ranking officer is the chief figure aboard ship.

clue.text: Excellent article about one socialist

indicators.note: the outer pieces go about, around, the inner one

parts.note: fab is slang for fabulous, excellent
an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A glowing newspaper profile of a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: A Fabian is a member of the Fabian Society, a British gradualist socialist group.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a gradualist socialist society founded in London in 1884.

clue.text: Type of power vibrato microphone needs

indicators.note: the phrase needs, so holds within it, the letters required

explanation.surface: A singer's vibrato needs a powerful microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is known by this adjective, as in nuclear-generated electricity.

clue.text: Cover over chicken with extra fat

parts.note: a cap is a cover, as on a bottle
on means over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: cover a fatty chicken before roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a plump bird.

clue.text: Self-confidence around masculine pub in time of Prohibition

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: ego is self-esteem or self-confidence
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Swagger in a men's bar during the US Prohibition era.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital-P 'Prohibition' points to the 1920s US alcohol ban; here it is just a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade or some activity is a prohibition.

clue.text: Being tall and thin is put right when cutting out metres

indicators.note: cutting out means removing the metres letter

parts.note: to remedy is to put right
M is the abbreviation for metres

explanation.surface: A tailor's comment: a lanky figure is fixed by trimming some metres off.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a reed, a person who is slender and lanky is described this way.

clue.text: Bad smell in central part of Madeira, perhaps

indicators.note: only the middle is kept, the outer letters dropped

parts.note: Madeira cake is an example of a plain sponge

explanation.surface: A foul whiff at the heart of the island of Madeira.
explanation.walkthrough: Madeira looks like the island or the wine; it is Madeira cake, a sponge. PONG is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a stink, an unpleasant odour.

clue.text: Noon leaves no gloomy lingering impression

indicators.note: the noon letter leaves, departs from, the phrase

parts.note: dour means sullen, gloomy

explanation.surface: Midday arrives and the gloom finally lifts, yet something lingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputation or impression that hangs about, as in an odour of sanctity.

clue.text: Love of what's posted recently on page with greeting

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece placed on another comes after it, so recently follows page and greeting

parts.note: hi is a greeting
lately means recently

explanation.surface: A social-media page greeting someone fond of what gets posted lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' suggests online posts; it means mailed letters, and so stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collecting is fondness for postage stamps, things that go through the mail.

clue.text: Western shootist in bar room, back to stay

indicators.note: back means the word for the small room is read in reverse

parts.note: a snug is a small private room in a British pub
to linger is to stay on

explanation.surface: A cowboy gunman in a saloon bar, back to stay a while.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small cosy room in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed gunman of the Wild West who shoots is the figure meant.

clue.text: One permanently late could be fired over this

definitions.text: One permanently late could be fired over this

parts.words: One permanently late could be fired over this
parts.note: someone permanently late is dead, the late so-and-so, and a corpse is burned on a funeral bonfire

explanation.surface: An employee always late for work might get the sack over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' reads as unpunctual and 'fired' as sacked; really the late means deceased, and fired means burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of wood on which a body is burned at a funeral.
